  • Search Post

  • User Detail

  • API Place Detail — {{base_url}}/places/detail/BAGB282c8c4c6a-lg20260605104956-bbb737a0d53d
    • allowed include filters:
      • location_name
      • location_post
      • thumbnail
      • total_posts
      • total_views
  • API Place Detail Post — {{base_url}}/places/detail/posts/BAGB282c8c4c6a-lg20260605104956-bbb737a0d53d?limit=2&page=1
    • allowed include filters:
      • slug
      • thumbnail
      • description
      • created_at
      • post_type
      • animation
      • little_planet

      • total_views
      • total_likes
      • total_comments

  • API Place Detail (Contributors) — {{base_url}}/places/detail/contributors/BAGB282c8c4c6a-lg20260605104956-bbb737a0d53d?limit=1&page=2
    • allowed include filters:
      • avatar
      • fullname
      • username
      • total_posts

  • For each endpoint, pass include=<fields> (only the fields the view actually needs) via the facade/service; confirm each field name against the allowed list above.

  • The timeline routes (foryou, recent, nearby, marzipano, etc.) are no longer present — likely replaced by home + place/detail-place.

SEO Audit: New Route URL Migration

Audit date: 2026-07-08
Scope: route migration from legacy Panorra URLs to the new Angular SSR/PWA flow
Primary source: this route map plus current router files in src/app
Business type detected: visual discovery / 360 panorama content platform
Overall route-SEO readiness score: 63 / 100

This score is for the migration plan and route implementation readiness, not a live production crawl. The current route map is directionally better than the legacy flow because it uses cleaner public content paths such as /post/:id, /:username, /place/:slug, /collection/:slug, and /potd/:slug. The main SEO risk is that old indexed URLs are not consistently redirected to the new canonical URLs.

Executive Summary

The new flow improves URL clarity, but the migration is not yet SEO-safe.

Top risks:

  1. Old high-value post URLs (/p/:slug) are not redirected to /post/:slug.
  2. Old viewer URLs (/view/:slug) are not redirected to /fullscreen/:slug.
  3. The sitemap still contains hashbang-style legacy URLs such as https://panorra.com/#/p/..., which conflict with the new non-hash SSR routes.
  4. Internal navigation still emits legacy paths in several places (/p/:slug, /page/notfound, /profile/:username, /bookmark).
  5. If /profile remains as a default route, it must not redirect to a hard-coded user such as /profile/jhonat.
  6. Dynamic content routes do not have a documented canonical/meta/schema strategy.

Top quick wins:

  1. Add server-level or Angular route redirects for all legacy public URLs.
  2. Update sitemap generation to emit canonical non-hash URLs.
  3. Replace all internal links and programmatic navigations that still use old routes.
  4. Add canonical tags for public post, profile, collection, place, and POTD detail pages.
  5. Remove private/authenticated settings and edit routes from indexable sitemap candidates.

Category Score Notes

Content Quality 70 Public content templates can rank, but route intent needs clearer page-level metadata.
On-Page SEO 60 Dynamic titles exist in limited places; canonical title/description rules are not mapped.
Schema / Structured Data 45 No route-level schema plan is documented for public content pages.
Performance / CWV 68 SSR helps, but panorama/fullscreen routes need careful deferral and image optimization.
AI Search Readiness 62 Clean route taxonomy helps, but pages need crawlable summaries and stable canonical URLs.
Images 70 Visual platform has strong assets; sitemap/image metadata strategy is missing.

Critical Findings

1. Legacy post URLs need permanent redirects

Legacy:

/p/:slug

New canonical:

/post/:slug

Impact:

  • Existing indexed post pages can become 404s.
  • External backlinks to shared posts lose value.
  • Search engines may treat legacy and new URLs as separate documents if both work without a canonical.

Recommendation:

  • Add a 301-equivalent redirect from /p/:slug to /post/:slug.
  • Update all internal navigation to use /post/:slug.
  • Keep the redirect for at least one full organic recrawl cycle.

Current evidence:

  • src/app/layout/layout.routes.ts defines /post/:id.
  • src/app/core/notification/post/post.component.ts still navigates to /p/${slug}.
  • src/app/components/post-thumbnail/post-link/post-link.component.ts still writes /p/${slug} through Location.go.
  • src/xml/sitemap.xml still lists https://panorra.com/#/p/....

2. Legacy fullscreen viewer URLs need permanent redirects

Legacy:

/view/:slug

New canonical:

/fullscreen/:slug

Impact:

  • Shared embed/viewer links can break.
  • Search engines may discover a dead route instead of the viewer route.

Recommendation:

  • Add redirect /view/:slug -> /fullscreen/:slug.
  • Decide whether /fullscreen/:slug should be indexable. If it is mostly an immersive viewer with thin text, canonical it to /post/:slug where the richer metadata and comments live.

3. Sitemap is still legacy and hash-based

Current sitemap pattern:

https://panorra.com/#/p/{slug}

New desired pattern:

https://panorra.com/post/{slug}
https://panorra.com/{username}
https://panorra.com/collection/{slug}
https://panorra.com/place/{place-slug}
https://panorra.com/potd/{slug}

Impact:

  • Hash URLs are weak crawl targets for modern SSR.
  • The sitemap points search engines at URLs that are not the new canonical route set.
  • Search engines receive mixed signals between sitemap, router, internal links, and SSR routes.

Recommendation:

  • Regenerate src/xml/sitemap.xml from public canonical routes only.
  • Remove all /#/p/ entries.
  • Do not include private routes such as /settings, /create, /edit-draft, /post/:id/edit-hotspot-banner, or /streetview/publish.
  • Add dynamic sitemap generation later if static XML cannot stay fresh.

4. Public profile URLs should use the short username route

Canonical:

/:username

Impact:

  • Short username URLs are cleaner, more memorable, and better aligned with social profile URL conventions.
  • The route can conflict with static top-level pages if route ordering and reserved-slug validation are not enforced.
  • Current code still contains navigation to /profile/:username in some places.

Recommendation:

  • Use /:username as the canonical profile URL.
  • Register /:username after all static public routes.
  • Maintain a reserved-slug list for routes like search, settings, potd, create, explore, restore, collection, post, fullscreen, and detail.
  • Update internal navigation from /profile/:username to /:username.

Current evidence:

  • Some code still navigates to /profile/${username}.

5. /profile should not redirect to a hard-coded user

Current new flow:

/profile -> /profile/jhonat

Impact:

  • Search engines and unauthenticated users may treat one user's profile as the default profile page.
  • This creates an artificial canonical signal for /profile.
  • It may expose implementation/demo data as a real SEO target.

Recommendation:

  • Replace /profile -> /profile/jhonat with one of:
    • /profile -> / for public users.
    • /profile -> /{currentUsername} only after browser/auth resolution, not as an SSR canonical redirect.
    • A noindex account/profile landing state if the page is only meaningful after login.

For every indexable dynamic route, set:

  • <title> from the entity name and route type.
  • <meta name="description"> from entity description/location.
  • <link rel="canonical"> to the exact clean URL.
  • Open Graph tags matching the canonical URL and thumbnail.
  • JSON-LD where appropriate.

If /fullscreen/:slug remains indexable, list it only when it has unique crawlable content and a self-canonical. Otherwise, let /post/:slug be the sitemap target.

Redirect Implementation Notes

Prefer server-level redirects in src/server.ts because search engines and social bots hit the server first. Angular client redirects are useful as a fallback, but server redirects give cleaner SEO signals.

Recommended server redirect rules:

/p/:slug -> /post/:slug
/view/:slug -> /fullscreen/:slug
/page/restore -> /restore
/settings/account -> /settings/user-account
/settings/block-user -> /settings/blocked-users
/settings/block-post -> /settings/blocked-posts

Routes needing validation/product decisions before redirecting:

/profile/:username -> /:username
/map -> /explore or /street-view
/hashtag?tag=... -> /search?tab=hashtags&q=...
/recent -> / or /explore
/nearby -> / or /explore
/location -> / or /explore

Do not redirect private/auth routes as permanent SEO URLs if the destination depends on login state. Use 302 or client-side authenticated routing for private pages.

Internal Link Cleanup Checklist

Known legacy references to update:

  • src/app/core/notification/post/post.component.ts: /p/${slug} should become /post/${slug}.
  • src/app/components/post-thumbnail/post-link/post-link.component.ts: Location.go('/p/' + slug) should become router navigation or Location.go('/post/' + slug).
  • src/app/pages/settings/bookmark/bookmark.component.ts: /page/notfound should become a real 404/wildcard navigation or an inline unavailable state.
  • src/app/pages/profile/profile.component.ts: /page/notfound should become a real 404/wildcard navigation or inline not-found state.
  • Code paths that navigate to /profile/${username} should become /${username}.
  • src/app/pages/profile/profile-settings-menu/profile-settings-menu.component.ts: /bookmark should become /settings/bookmark.

SSR / PWA Notes

  • Keep all public route pages SSR-safe: no unguarded window, document, or localStorage in route/container components.
  • Use RenderMode.Server for public SEO pages that need fresh metadata.
  • Use noindex meta for authenticated settings, create, edit, and draft pages.
  • Do not rely on service-worker cached legacy HTML for redirects. Redirects should happen before Angular bootstraps where possible.

Acceptance Criteria

The route migration is SEO-ready when:

  • /p/:slug returns a permanent redirect to /post/:slug.
  • /view/:slug returns a permanent redirect to /fullscreen/:slug or the chosen canonical destination.
  • Public profile URLs resolve at /:username, with reserved static route names protected and invalid usernames returning a correct not-found status.
  • Sitemap contains only canonical non-hash URLs.
  • All public dynamic pages emit stable title, description, canonical, OG, and schema metadata.
  • Private/settings/create/edit routes are excluded from sitemap and marked noindex.
  • Internal links no longer generate legacy public paths.
  • 404/unavailable content returns the correct status or a clearly non-indexable unavailable state.

Prioritized Action Plan

  1. Implement server redirects for /p/:slug, /view/:slug, and /page/restore.
  2. Regenerate sitemap without /#/p/ URLs.
  3. Replace internal legacy post/profile links.

  2. Decide whether /fullscreen/:slug is indexable or canonicalizes to /post/:slug.
  3. Remove /profile -> /profile/jhonat as an SSR/public default redirect.

  1. Add redirects for settings route renames.
  2. Define product mapping for old discovery routes (/map, /location, /recent, /nearby, /hashtag).
  3. Add JSON-LD for public content routes.

  1. Retire /report/* from all public route documentation.
  2. Keep route docs synced with app.routes.server.ts.
  3. Document the sitemap generation process so it does not drift again.

issues.display_title: Issue #3071: Restructure File Architecture and Remove Deprecated Components
issues.main_description_html:
🧹 Restructure File Architecture and Remove Deprecated Components

Tidy the pages-new codebase: align folders/files to the established per-feature contract and remove deprecated/legacy components no longer used by the new flow.

Based on pages-new. Context: docs/brainstorming/09-06-2026/analyze-new.md (§9 mock surfaces, roadmap #10 "retire pages-old after parity").

Scope

  • Restructure pages-new features to the file contract: *.component.ts/html/scss · *.routes.ts · *.facade.ts / *-ui.service.ts · *.api.model.ts · *.mapper.ts · *.viewmodel.ts. Consistent folder naming; co-locate files that change together.
  • Remove deprecated components / dead code that the new flow no longer references (and the matching commented-out routes in layout.routes.ts).
  • Replace remaining mock *.data.ts where the feature is already API-wired, or clearly mark the ones still pending (detail-post.data.ts, explore.data.ts, home-places.data.ts, home-photographers.data.ts, profile.data.ts).
  • Enforce conventions: standalone: true, ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush, signals (no BehaviorSubject), facade for I/O, no any.
  • Do not delete pages-old wholesale unless parity is confirmed — only remove what's provably unused.

Verification (must pass before done)

  • npx ng build --configuration dev succeeds (no unresolved imports after moves/removals).
  • npm run lint — no new errors; confirm no any / BehaviorSubject reintroduced.
  • No broken routes — every active route in layout.routes.ts / feature *.routes.ts still resolves.
  • Quick smoke: home, post detail, create, profile, settings, fullscreen still load.
  • Removed files are confirmed unreferenced (grep for imports before deleting).

Out of scope

  • Full pages-old retirement (separate, post-parity task).
  • New features / behavior changes — this is structure + cleanup only.

Acceptance: pages-new follows the file contract consistently; provably-unused deprecated components/routes removed; build + lint green; no route or smoke regressions; no any.

Detail update by developen

Branch Changes: enhancment-arsitektir-file vs origin/dev

Scope: 13 commits, 1104 files changed, +1216/−84295 lines (verified against origin/dev, the actual merge-base — master has diverged too far to be a meaningful comparison).

Summary

This branch is primarily a large dead-code purge: it removes the legacy pages-old/ tree, a duplicated legacy panorama/dialog widget tree under core/ and shared/, and the last remnants of the NgModule-based bootstrap (app.module.ts, layout.module.ts). It also finishes the pages-new → pages rename and rolls out ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush across ~58 components. It is not risk-free cleanup — deleting pages-old orphaned several service dependencies, and instead of rewiring them, the calling code was commented out, silently disabling real features.

Architecture changes

  • app.module.ts deleted; its providers (PathLocationStrategy, NgxScrollPositionRestorationModule, provideZoneChangeDetection) moved into app.config.ts — standalone bootstrap finalized, functionally equivalent.
  • app-routing.module.ts drops routes to now-deleted modules (view/:slug, page/maps, report, p/:slug, page/unavailable-post).
  • layout.routes.ts changes are cleanup of already-dead commented-out route registrations, not live removals.

Deletions (confirmed dead, no dangling imports)

  • Entire src/app/pages-old/** (bookmark, ~5000-line create-post, fullscreen, nearest, post-detail, profile/profile_old, panorra-report admin panel, settings, timeline, legal).
  • Duplicate legacy panorama tree in core/components/** and shared/components/** (view-panorama ~3355 lines, post-panorama ~730 lines ×2, menu-panorama, video-player ~794 lines, youtube-player, aspect-ratio, filter-panorama, suggestion, sub-header). The actively used copy at src/app/components/panorama/** only received small OnPush edits — confirms these were stale forks.
  • src/app/shared/modals/** — duplicates of src/app/components/dialogs/** (the tree that's actually wired up).
  • src/app/core/header/, core/sidebar/, core/most-popular/, core/sub-header/, core/suggestion/, core/notification/menu-settings/ — no replacement found, appears genuinely dead.
  • components/panorama/menu-post/ (464 lines) — only consumers were in the deleted trees, so removal is clean.
  • src/app/interfeces/** — no dangling imports, but some typed usages were downgraded to any rather than repointed to new .model.ts types (type-safety loss, see below).

Renames/restructuring

pages-new → pages: mostly pure moves. Files with real edits beyond the rename:

  • pages/pages.service.ts (verified directly) — real-time sync logic commented out in refresessPost, refressPostTimeline, refresessUsers, actionPostTimeline. Cross-view like/bookmark/comment-count sync between recent/foryou/nearby/profile timelines is disabled.
  • comment-list.component.ts — mostly Prettier reformatting; one stray console.log('value', value) left in addComment().
  • action-follow.component.ts, home.facade.ts, detail-social.component.ts, place.component.ts, potd-detail.component.ts — mostly reformatting/OnPush additions.

Behavioral changes (real regressions, not just cleanup)

  1. OnPush rollout (~58 components) — real strategy change; components mutating plain objects/arrays without signals or markForCheck() may stop re-rendering.
  2. view-panorama.component.html — *ngIf → @if (template syntax only, no behavior change).
  3. Orphaned-service regressions (functions silently no-op'd instead of rewired):
    • list-like-post.component.ts (verified directly) — the "who liked this comment" dialog is fully non-functional; PostDetailService injection and all its calls are commented out.
    • menu-panorama.component.ts — fullscreen action no longer forwards static post data.
    • post-link.component.ts — clicking a post no longer opens the post-detail modal with static data.
    • comment-post.component.ts — comment counter falls back to a local signal instead of the cross-view synced counter.
    • core/notification/drafts/drafts.component.ts — "Edit draft" no longer engages CreatePostService's edit mode; type downgraded to any.

Risk / impact on the running app

  • No dangling compile-time imports found (pages-old, interfeces, AppModule all clear) — but an actual ng build --configuration production has not been run as part of this analysis and should be, to be certain.
  • The real risk is silent feature loss that still compiles: comment-like dialogs, draft editing, fullscreen static-data handoff, and cross-timeline sync are functionally broken in this branch despite no build errors.
  • Bundle size should shrink meaningfully (~84K deleted lines, including the 5000-line legacy create-post component and 3300-line duplicate view-panorama).
  • OnPush across 58 components needs targeted QA, particularly for any component still mutating state imperatively rather than via signals.

Testing recommendations

  1. Like/bookmark a post in one timeline view, confirm counts update in other open views (currently likely broken).
  2. Open "who liked this comment" — confirm it's known-broken or needs a follow-up fix.
  3. Click "Edit" on a draft — confirm create-post edit mode still engages.
  4. Test fullscreen entry from a post-link click and from the panorama menu's fullscreen action.
  5. Run ng build --configuration production to catch anything a grep sweep would miss.
  6. Spot-check several OnPush-converted components for missed UI updates.
